tried: New mechanism class (2026-07-30): instead of decoding EMG into a target action, shape the *covariance* of MPO's exploration noise using the real cross-actuator EMG correlation matrix (Cholesky factor L, perturbation = noise_scale*(L@eps)). Swept noise_scale (0.02/0.05/0.15), intervention_proba (0.1 vs 0.5), mirror_left, and a temporal_corr (AR(1)/OU) extension for time-smoothness. h0918, plain reward.
result: Real vs null indistinguishable at every single setting tried -- 8 runs, all landing in a tight 9090-9200 band. shuffle_corr and temporal_corr=0.95 pair were launched but deliberately aborted before completion once the pattern was already clear from 8 prior runs.
why_not: No hyperparameter combination ever separated real from null; judged very unlikely shuffle_corr would separate from an already-flat baseline. More likely root cause: corrnoise perturbs the *executed* action post-hoc, so MPO's own policy distribution never treats it as native (unlike true Lattice/gSDE, which reshapes the sampling distribution directly -- ruled out as a same-session build, needs new trust-region math for a correlated Gaussian).

tried: Third mechanism class (2026-08-02): reward the policy's own recent muscle-activation history (rolling 50-step window) for matching real EMG's cross-actuator correlation structure, via imitation_coeff*(-MSE vs target correlation matrix) added to the base reward. h0918, real/null(identity)/shuffle(permuted) targets, single seed each.
result: Real 9101.2, null(identity) 9186.4, shuffle 9103.2 -- null nominally highest, all three within ~85pts of each other and of plain MPO (~9108.7). A real bug was caught and fixed first: cosine-similarity made the null target mathematically vacuous (identically 0 regardless of input); switched to negative MSE to make it a genuine matched control.
why_not: Extends the same flat/reversed pattern already seen on the action channel (free-blend, corrnoise) to a third, structurally distinct mechanism class (reward, not action) -- real vs null still doesn't separate in EMG's favor regardless of which channel carries the mechanism.

ablation: Self-derived synergy prior (SAR-style, decoder fit on the policy's own rollout instead of EMG)
tried: Fits a k=11 synergy decoder on a trained MPO checkpoint's own greedy rollout activations (not EMG) -- isolates whether the project's mechanisms need biological content specifically or just any self-consistent low-dimensional structure. Full-coverage (all 18 actuators), residual_weight=0.1 (matches hardconstraint11), h0918, single seed real/null, plus a shuffled-decoder control added later.
result: Real: 9237.8 (best stable h0918 score on record). Null (a_hat=0, same blanket 10% clamp): 464.1, a near-total collapse. Shuffle (real decoder's own output values reattached to the wrong actuators): 8790.9 -- far closer to real than to null.
why_not: The shuffle control shows the real-vs-null gap is mostly about having *any* structured nonzero content under a blanket full-actuator clamp (the same 'structured beats nothing' pattern as the untrained-decoder findings elsewhere), not evidence for self-derived-synergy content specifically. Not carried forward as its own mechanism.

tried: Combine DEP's online self-organizing exploration with the EMG hard-constraint mechanism, to try to beat DEP-MPO outright (config-only: dep_factory(0,...) -> dep_factory(3,...) on existing hardconstraint configs).
result: Crashed on a real structural incompatibility (not a config bug): einsum dimension mismatch, DEP's C-matrix assumes the action dimension and sensed muscle-state dimension are the same 1:1 space (18=18 for h0918); LatentActionPriorWrapper breaks this by making the action space 29-dim (11 latent + 18 residual) while muscle-state sensing stays 18-dim.
why_not: Architecturally blocked, not an afternoon fix -- would require redefining how DEP's C-matrix relates actions to muscle states for a non-1:1 space, a real research question in itself. Never revisited.

ablation: Coverage-tracking hypothesis (does EMG-actuator-coverage fraction predict real-vs-null win direction under the hard constraint)

ablation: Gait-phase-conditioning for the decoder (AE_phase vs plain AE, held-out R2)
tried: Added sin/cos phase-of-gait-cycle as a conditioning input to the synergy autoencoder (phase derived for free from the h5's own 101-point-per-stride layout), k=1..11 sweep.
result: Phase-conditioning helps a lot at low k (+0.127 R2 at k=1) but the gain vanishes/reverses by k=8-11 (-0.006 to -0.011) -- exactly the k range the actual RL work uses.
why_not: At k=11 the AE already has as many latent dims as EMG channels, so it doesn't need phase as a reconstruction shortcut -- not actionable for the k=6/11 RL work; the coverage-gap / missing-forcing-function stories remain the more likely explanation for whatever phase-conditioning would have addressed.

ablation: Phase-conditioned VAE for structured exploration noise (train_phase_vae.py)
tried: A phase-conditioned generative decoder sampling z~N(0,I) at a fixed gait phase, intended to produce naturally cross-muscle-correlated, phase-appropriate exploration noise for MPO -- the same mechanism Lattice hand-engineers, learned from real EMG instead. Beta-KL sweep (1.0, 0.1, 0.05, 0.3) at decoder level only, no RL integration attempted.
result: beta=0.05 is the standout: held-out R2=0.840 (near the deterministic AE_phase ceiling of 0.888), with clean, anatomically sensible correlation structure (vastusmedialis~vastuslateralis and bicepsfemoris~semitendinosus both 0.98-1.00 at every phase point). beta=0.3 looked stronger on raw correlation (0.75-0.96) but was diagnosed as posterior collapse, not genuine structure. beta=1.0 was simply too aggressive a KL weight.
why_not: Worth writing up as a real supplementary finding at the decoder level, but full MPO-noise integration would require replacing GaussianPolicyHead (MPO's actual noise source, per-actuator independent Gaussian by construction) with a new custom actor class touching shared/vendored code -- a separate, larger, riskier engineering task, never scoped or attempted.

ablation: Data-efficiency (steps-to-threshold) analysis, free-blend vs hard-constraint groups
tried: wandb-history-only analysis (no new training): steps to reach fixed score thresholds (6000/7000/8000/8500), free-blend (w=0.5, k=3/6/11) vs hard-constraint (k=11, mapped_residual_weight=0.1) groups, h0918.
result: Free-blend: no consistent data-efficiency edge for real EMG -- k=11 real/null reach every threshold within ~200k steps of each other; plain MPO reaches 8000 fastest of all (2.2-2.4M steps), likely just its smaller action space. tried: Full 4-arm design: per-episode target_vel~U[0.8,1.5], symmetric gaussianVel reward, normalized target speed in obs. vcond_real (speed-conditioned EMG decoder, decoder(z,v)->EMG) / vcond_null (a_hat=0, speed still in obs) / uncond_real (plain treadmill-pool decoder, no speed input) / mpo_baseline (no wrapper). h0918, 10M steps, kill-switch review at 5M. Held-out-speed eval harness (leaps.scripts.eval_vcond_heldout_speed): pin target_vel to {0.6,0.9,1.1,1.3,1.6,1.8}, 20 eps/speed, on step_6000000.
result: seed0 finished at 10M: vcond_real 970.0, vcond_null 973.9, mpo_baseline 972.6 -- 4-point spread, dead heat. seed1/uncond partials all 966-974 (converged since 2M). Held-out eval: interpolation speeds all three ~equal (970-987); extrapolation all three fail identically -- top speed saturates ~1.37 m/s regardless of prior, 0.6 missed by all. uncond_real (static-prior contrast) 973.7, also on top of everything. Only real difference: vcond_real muscle activations smooth/low/unsaturated (mean ~0.07) vs vcond_null/mpo_baseline bang-bang (mean ~0.35, max 1.0).
why_not: Clean null on the one body tested. mpo_baseline is DEP-MPO + AdaptiveEnergyBuffer (already a strong exploration prior); reward is trivially saturable (vel_coeff=1, every other coeff 0, no effort/style term) so coordinated activation isn't rewarded; h0918 + a 1-parameter gait family is easy -> no room for an inductive bias. Same failure mode as fixed-speed (real EMG ~= null); task breadth didn't make h0918 hard enough. All jobs killed 2026-08-27, queue.txt block commented out. Kept as a negative finding supporting the reframe (prior's value is plausibility, not return). A full h1622/h2190 sweep would be a new experiment against the 'no new experiments after vcond' plan.
